column1: # German explicit terms — page-text scoring tier.
# Format:  term<TAB>weight     (see terms.en.tsv for what the weights mean)
# `Amateursex` are single words. That makes this language unusually rewarding
# for a filter — one stem catches a whole family — and unusually dangerous,
# because the same property produces `Nacktschnecke` (a slug), `Nacktmull`
# The tokenizer splits on non-letters, so a solid compound is ONE token and a
# stem does not match it. That is the safe default and it is why the entries
# below list the compounds people actually write rather than relying on stems.
# ── THE TRAP: EVERYDAY WORDS THAT ARE ALSO EXPLICIT ────────────────────────
# German has several words whose ordinary sense is far more common than the
# explicit one. Each is listed at a LOW weight, never enough to block alone,
# with the innocent sense carried in negatives.tsv:
#   geil      youth slang for "great" — overwhelmingly the common use
#   spritzen  to inject — ordinary medical vocabulary
#   pissen    to urinate — crude, not adult content
# `test_terms.py` pins the negatives that keep medical and veterinary pages
# ═══ everyday words with an explicit second sense — LOW on purpose ═════════
# See the header. These carry weight only in company; negatives.tsv cancels
# them on veterinary, medical and ordinary pages.
